A 55-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus presents with complaints of fatigue, dark
urine, and bilateral leg heaviness for one week. She recently returned from a two-week trip to Rio de
Janeiro where she walked extensively and gained 7 pounds. Her only medication is
hydroxychloroquine. Physical examination reveals a temperature of 37.5°C (99.5°F), pulse of 79/min,
blood pressure of 175/87 mm Hg, and bilateral 2+ pretibial edema. Her urinalysis shows: | Blood | 3+ | |

--- | --- | | Protein | 1+ | | RBC | 6–8/hpf with dysmorphic features | | RBC casts | numerous | | WBC |
8/hpf | | WBC casts | rare | | Bacteria | negative | What is the most likely etiology of her leg findings?
Answer Choices: (A) Decreased cardiac output (B) Salt retention (C) Venous insufficiency (D)
Decreased renal blood flow (E) Renal protein loss (F) Decreased plasma oncotic pressure (G)
Lymphatic obstruction (H) Inflammatory vasculitis (I) Increased peripheral capillary permeability (J)
Deep venous thrombosis
 A. Decreased renal blood flow
B. Deep venous thrombosis
C. Renal protein loss
D. Venous insufficiency
E. Decreased plasma oncotic pressure
F. Inflammatory vasculitis
